problem: End-to-end LSTM target-driven navigation policies keep no explicit spatial memory, while learned-map approaches assume perfect localization and rarely store semantic information. Localization-oriented maps such as MapNet use only RGB features.
motivation: Semantic target navigation (e.g. go to the couch) needs a spatial memory of where objects were seen, and that memory must work without ground-truth pose. Recognition outputs such as detections and segmentation are more view-invariant than raw RGB features, so they should help both re-localization and policy learning.
key_idea: Extend MapNet's allocentric 2.5D learned map with semantic segmentation and object-detection grids, and feed the map plus predicted pose to a supervised (DAgger) navigation policy that is jointly fine-tuned with the map.
insight: Semantic-only map features (SSeg-Det) localize best (AVD APE-20 647 mm vs 800 mm for RGB), because RGB embeddings must be view-invariant to match the egocentric grid to the allocentric map. On AVD the semantic-only map also gives the best navigation (64.6 vs 60.1 SR for RGB). On synthetic Matterport3D noisy detections make RGB+SSeg+Det best. Freezing the map costs 2-5 SR points, and removing egocentric observations costs about 4 points.
method: Ground projection: depth and intrinsics lift RGB CNN features (max-pooled), Faster R-CNN detection masks (averaged) and NYUv2 segmentation probabilities into an egocentric 21x21 grid, 300 mm cells.
Per-modality small CNNs: two conv layers per grid, stacked into the egocentric grid g_t.
Registration: cross-correlate g_t with map m_{t-1} over positions and 12 rotations, then softmax to get the pose distribution p_t. Deconvolution with p_t places g_t into map coordinates.
Map update: per-cell LSTM update of the 29x29 allocentric map (better than feature averaging). Trained with cross-entropy localization loss against GT pose.

Navigation policy: CNN embeddings of the map, p_t, egocentric observation (ResNet18), one-hot target and collision bit go to a 512-unit LSTM that predicts per-action cost. L1 loss on the cost (-1/0/1, collision 1, goal -2).
Training: online DAgger on a discrete pose graph, with shortest-path expert and random-walk episodes and exponentially decaying expert probability. The map module is fine-tuned jointly.
Controller: sample actions from a softmax over negated predicted costs.

setting.backbone: MapNet-style semantic map (ResNet50 truncated + small CNNs + LSTM) with CNN+LSTM policy (ResNet18), trained; frozen Faster R-CNN and NYUv2 segmentation model as inputs
setting.training_data: AVD: 33k random-walk episodes for localization, 55k initial DAgger episodes, 11 train and 3 test scenes. Matterport3D: 88k episodes, 17 train and 5 test scenes rendered via Habitat-Sim on a 30 cm grid.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with detection masks and semantic segmentation; a collision bit
setting.action_space: discrete graph moves (forward/backward/left/right/rotate ±30°), no stop action
setting.simulator: AVD (real images on a graph) and Matterport3D via Habitat-Sim rendered discrete graph
setting.privileged: GT pose for localization supervision in training only; at test time the graph gives depth. The non-learning baseline has full graph knowledge.

numbers.eval_set_note: 3 held-out scenes (Mousavian et al. split), 5 targets, max 100 steps
numbers.extra: no synthetic SUNCG data; success = within 5 steps of a target pose; no stop action

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks (AVD, graph-based Matterport3D), not canonical ones. Matterport3D APE-20 for SSeg-Det is 655 mm (RGB 993 mm).
results: On AVD the method reaches 64.6% SR, 10.6 points above the best learned no-map baseline (No-Map-SUNCG, 54.0), even without synthetic data. On Matterport3D it reaches 69.5% SR vs 42.8% for the non-learning baseline. Semantic maps also reduce localization error relative to RGB-only maps.
limitations: Discrete graph environments with a fixed 30 cm grid and depth-based ground projection; not continuous control or real robot
Only five object categories; depends on noisy off-the-shelf detectors and segmentation, with GT pose supervision needed
Baselines are limited; the path length ratio is not comparable with stop-action baselines
builds_on: Mousavian et al. visual representations for semantic target driven navigation
